questions.question_text: Which protected class is unique to West Virginia's Fair Housing Act and listed separately from general disability?
questions.explanation: §16B-18-5 lists blindness as its own protected characteristic alongside disability, so West Virginia protects blind applicants explicitly rather than folding them into a general disability category. Age, marital status and sexual orientation are not protected characteristics under the West Virginia Fair Housing Act.

questions.question_text: West Virginia's Fair Housing Act adds which protected class that is NOT in the federal Fair Housing Act?
questions.explanation: §16B-18-5 protects ancestry in addition to national origin; the federal Fair Housing Act covers national origin but not ancestry as a separate class. Color, familial status and national origin are all already federal classes.

questions.question_text: How many protected classes are covered under West Virginia's Fair Housing Act?
questions.explanation: §16B-18-5 lists nine: race, color, religion, ancestry, sex, familial status, blindness, disability and national origin. Note the current wording is "disability" — defined at §16B-18-3(g) — rather than the older term "handicap." The federal Fair Housing Act covers seven, lacking ancestry and a separate blindness class.

questions.question_text: A landlord refuses to rent to a tenant because the tenant is blind. Under WV law, is this discrimination?
questions.correct_answer: Yes, blindness is a protected class in WV
distractors: Only if the landlord receives federal funding
Only if the property has 5 or more units
No, blindness falls under disability only
questions.explanation: Blindness is specifically enumerated as a separate protected class under WV's Fair Housing Act, providing explicit protection beyond the general handicap/disability category.

questions.question_text: A property owner discriminates against a prospective buyer based on their Italian ancestry. Is this a violation under WV law?
questions.correct_answer: Yes, ancestry is a WV protected class
distractors: Only if it also involves national origin
No, ancestry is not a WV protected class
Only in rental situations, not sales
questions.explanation: Ancestry is a protected class under WV's Fair Housing Act, separate from national origin. Discrimination based on Italian ancestry violates both state and potentially federal law.

questions.question_text: An agent steers minority buyers away from certain neighborhoods. Under WV law, this is an example of what?
questions.correct_answer: Steering — a prohibited fair housing practice
distractors: Good customer service to match preferences
questions.explanation: Steering is a prohibited practice under WV's Fair Housing Act. Directing buyers toward or away from neighborhoods based on protected characteristics is illegal.

questions.question_text: A real estate agent tells homeowners in a neighborhood that property values will drop because families of a different race are moving in. What violation is this?
questions.explanation: §16B-18-5(e) makes it unlawful, "for profit, to induce or attempt to induce any person to sell or rent any dwelling by representations regarding the entry or prospective entry into the neighborhood" of persons of a protected class. Note the statutory element: the inducement must be for profit. Steering directs buyers toward or away from areas; redlining is the denial of lending or related services.

questions.question_text: A WV property listing states 'no children allowed.' Under the Fair Housing Act, what type of discrimination is this?
distractors: Not a violation for rental properties
Legal if the property is unsafe for children
questions.explanation: Familial status is protected by §16B-18-5 and defined at §16B-18-3(j) to cover individuals under 18 domiciled with a parent or legal custodian, and any person who is pregnant or securing legal custody. The exception is "housing for older persons" under §16B-18-8(b)(2): housing under a qualifying state or federal elderly program, housing intended for and solely occupied by persons 62 or older, or housing for 55 and older where at least 80 percent of the units have an occupant 55 or older, with significant facilities and services for older persons and published policies showing that intent.

questions.question_text: A lending institution refuses to make loans for properties in certain neighborhoods based on racial composition. This practice is called what?
questions.explanation: Redlining is the practice of denying services (especially lending) based on the racial or ethnic composition of a neighborhood. It is a prohibited fair housing practice.

questions.question_text: A WV broker denies a licensee access to the local MLS based on the licensee's religion. What violation has occurred?
questions.correct_answer: Denial of access to real estate services
distractors: No violation since MLSs are private
Only a violation if religion affects competency
A violation of WVREC advertising rules only
questions.explanation: §16B-18-7 makes it unlawful "to deny any person access to or membership or participation in any multiple listing service, real estate broker's organization or other service, organization or facility relating to the business of selling or renting dwellings," or to discriminate in the terms of that access, on account of any protected characteristic — religion included. That an MLS is privately operated is no defence.

questions.question_text: Which state agency enforces the WV Fair Housing Act?
questions.explanation: §16B-18-9: "The authority and responsibility for administering this article shall be in the West Virginia Human Rights Commission." The Commission now sits within the state's Office of the Inspector General. The WVREC regulates real estate licensure and can discipline a licensee for discriminating, but it does not administer the Fair Housing Act.

questions.question_text: What powers does the WV Human Rights Commission have regarding fair housing complaints?
questions.correct_answer: Investigate, hold hearings, and order remedies
distractors: Only accept and forward complaints to HUD
Only issue advisory opinions without enforcement
questions.explanation: The Commission investigates, conciliates, holds hearings through administrative law judges who must be licensed attorneys, and orders relief (§§16B-18-9, 16B-18-11, 16B-18-13). An aggrieved person must file within one year of the alleged practice, and the Commission must generally complete its investigation and make a reasonable-cause determination within 100 days. An ALJ may award actual damages and injunctive or other equitable relief, plus civil penalties of up to $10,000, $25,000 or $50,000 depending on the respondent's history, and may allow a prevailing complainant attorney's fees and costs.

questions.question_text: A homebuyer experiences housing discrimination in WV. Where can they file a complaint?
questions.correct_answer: WV Human Rights Commission, HUD, or state court
distractors: Only with the WV Human Rights Commission
Only with HUD in Washington DC
questions.explanation: All three routes exist: an administrative complaint with the Human Rights Commission, a HUD complaint, or a civil action in circuit court. The deadlines differ — one year for the administrative complaint (§16B-18-11(a)(1)(A)) but two years for a private circuit-court action (§16B-18-14(a)(1)(A)). They are not cumulative once a charge issues: §16B-18-13 sets out an election of remedies, under which a party may elect to have the claims in the charge decided in a civil action in lieu of an administrative hearing, and must make that election within 20 days of service.

questions.question_text: A person files a fair housing complaint with the WV Human Rights Commission. What happens next?
distractors: The complainant must hire an attorney first
The case goes directly to a jury trial
questions.explanation: The Commission investigates, and §16B-18-11 requires it to complete the investigation and determine whether reasonable cause exists within 100 days of filing, notifying the parties in writing if it cannot. Conciliation is attempted throughout. The complaint itself must have been filed within one year of the alleged discriminatory housing practice.

questions.question_text: A WV real estate licensee violates the Fair Housing Act. Which entities could take action against the licensee?
questions.correct_answer: Both the Human Rights Commission and the WVREC
distractors: Only the WV Human Rights Commission
Only the WVREC for license discipline
Only a civil court for monetary damages
questions.explanation: The Human Rights Commission enforces the Fair Housing Act (§16B-18-9), and §30-40-19(a)(27) independently makes it a ground for WVREC discipline to discriminate "against any person involved in a real estate transaction which is in violation of any federal or state anti-discrimination law, including any fair housing law." One discriminatory act can therefore cost both damages and the licence.
